answers_by_date.basis: In force: Constitution art. 14 (every inhabitant may 'enseñar y aprender') and art. 75 inc. 22, which gives the CRC and ICESCR constitutional rank; and Ley 24.195 art. 3, which guarantees access to education 'a toda la población'. Ley 22.439 art. 102 barred irregular foreigners only from secondary and higher schools ('enseñanza media o superior'), not from primary. Practice: art. 104 obliged public bodies to report irregular residents, and press accounts (La Nación 1999; Página/12 2003, citing CELS) document schools reporting families and children losing school years over their parents' irregular status.

Ley 25.871 took effect on publication (21 Jan 2004). Its art. 7 provides that 'en ningún caso la irregularidad migratoria' prevents admission as a pupil at any level, and art. 124 repealed Ley 22.439 together with its art. 102/104 reporting regime. The law was still unregulated. I could not open any practice source for c. 2005 (the CELS 2005 report PDF failed to load), so this rating is inferred.

Ley 25.871 arts. 6-7 were unchanged. From January 2007 two further provisions applied: Ley 26.206 art. 4 (free education for all inhabitants) and its final migrants clause (now art. 143), which guarantees access, continued attendance and completion for migrants without a DNI on the strength of documents from their country of origin. Practice: the CMW (2011) credits the law but notes 'discrimination against migrant children at school', and the CRC (2010) records rising enrolment. Decreto 616/2010 came only in May 2010.

Same provisions, plus Decreto 616/2010 art. 7 (May 2010), which tells the Ministry of Education to guarantee access for foreigners 'aún en situación de irregularidad migratoria'. DNU 70/2017 did not touch arts. 6-7, so nothing changed before 2020. Practice evidence for c. 2015 is thin: the CMW 2011 findings point to discrimination with access generally honoured. This matches the starting rating of 2020.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 but they are not the same

provisions.article: Art. 14; art. 75 inc. 22 (CRC art. 28, ICESCR art. 13 with constitutional rank)
Art. 4; art. 143 (printed as a second 'art. 141' in the original text)

provisions.instrument: Ley 22.439 General de Migraciones y de Fomento de la Inmigración

events.what_changed: Replaced Ley 22.439, which barred irregular foreigners only from secondary and higher schools and obliged public bodies to report them. The new art. 7 says irregular status can never prevent admission at any level, primary included.
events.passage: ARTICULO 7° — En ningún caso la irregularidad migratoria de un extranjero impedirá su admisión como alumno en un establecimiento educativo, ya sea este público o privado; nacional, provincial o municipal; primario, secundario, terciario o universitario.

events.what_changed: Repealed Ley 22.439, ending the enrolment restriction for secondary and higher education and the duty of officials to report irregular residents.
events.passage: ARTICULO 102. – Los institutos de enseñanza media o superior, ya sean públicos o privados, nacionales, provinciales o municipales, solamente podrán admitir como alumnos, a aquellos extranjeros que acrediten, para cada curso lectivo, su calidad de 'residentes permanentes' o 'residentes temporarios'

events.article: Art. 4; final migrants article (art. 143); art. 132 repealing Ley 24.195
events.what_changed: Free education for all inhabitants, and a specific guarantee of access, continued attendance and completion at all levels for migrants without a DNI. Replaced Ley 24.195.
events.passage: El Estado nacional, las provincias y la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires deberán garantizar a las personas migrantes sin Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI), el acceso y las condiciones para la permanencia y el egreso de todos los niveles del sistema educativo, mediante la presentación de documentos emanados de su país de origen

events.what_changed: Regulation of Ley 25.871 art. 7: the Ministry of Education must ensure that irregular foreigners have access to every level of education.
events.passage: ARTICULO 7º.- El MINISTERIO DE EDUCACION dictará las normas y dispondrá las medidas necesarias para garantizar a los extranjeros, aún en situación de irregularidad migratoria, el acceso a los distintos niveles educativos con el alcance previsto en la Ley Nº 26.206.

events.what_changed: After 2020 and outside the period: art. 7 now covers initial, primary and secondary schooling only, and art. 6 is tied to each migratory category. Primary schooling for irregular migrants remains protected.
events.passage: Los extranjeros tendrán derecho, aun cuando su condición migratoria fuera irregular, a ser admitidos como alumnos en un establecimiento educativo inicial, primario o secundario

answers.sourcing_note: I read the original texts of Ley 25.871, Ley 26.206 and Decreto 616/2010 and the texts of Ley 22.439 and Ley 24.195 on InfoLEG and argentina.gob.ar, so the dating of the law is strong. Practice evidence for 2005 and 2015 is thin: the CELS annual reports and the CAREF study are PDFs that could not be opened.
answers.notes: The 2000 answer rests on the CRC and ICESCR, which have constitutional rank under art. 75 inc. 22 and are directly applicable, together with Ley 24.195. Ley 22.439 restricted only secondary and higher education. The Ley Videla reporting duty and the documented exclusions bear on implementation, not on the protection answer. No rulings were relied on. Buenos Aires City Ley 203 (1999) is subnational and was not counted.
